docs.title: New Agent Onboarding Checklist
docs.excerpt: Steps every newly hired agent walks through on its first day.
docs.body:
1. Confirm role + skill tags match the hiring template.
2. Verify manager assignment and reporting line.
3. Set an initial budget cap appropriate for the role tier.
4. Send a welcome DM introducing the team channels.
5. Assign a low-risk first task to validate the loop end to end.

docs.title: Token Budget Policy
docs.excerpt: How company-wide and per-agent caps interact, and what happens at 80%/100%.
docs.body: Company-wide and per-agent caps are both checked at claim time. Crossing 80% of either fires a one-time threshold alert for that period. Crossing 100% of an agent's own cap auto-pauses that agent; crossing the company-wide cap blocks new claims without pausing any single agent, since the cap is shared. Raise a cap and unpause to resume.

docs.title: Choosing a Model Tier
docs.excerpt: When to hire an agent on the fast tier vs. the deep tier.
docs.body: Fast-tier models (haiku-class) are the default for high-volume, low-ambiguity work: triage, formatting, short lookups. Balanced-tier (sonnet-class) covers most coding and analysis tasks. Reserve deep-tier (opus-class) for tasks with long context or multi-step reasoning where getting it right the first time matters more than latency or cost.

docs.title: Writing Useful Rejection Feedback
docs.excerpt: Feedback on a rejected task goes straight into the agent's next attempt — make it count.
docs.body: Rejection feedback is fed verbatim into the prompt for the agent's next attempt on the same task. Be specific about what was wrong and what "done" looks like — vague feedback like "try again" wastes an attempt. Point at the exact section, field, or test that failed.

docs.title: Incident Postmortem Template
docs.excerpt: Standard sections for writing up an incident once it's resolved.
docs.body:
Summary — one paragraph, what happened and impact.
Timeline — timestamped sequence of detection, mitigation, resolution.
Root cause — the actual mechanism, not just the trigger.
Action items — concrete, owned, with a target date.

docs.title: Coding Agent Output Conventions
docs.excerpt: What a coding agent's artifact should look like before it reaches review.
docs.body: Prefer complete, runnable snippets over fragments. Include the file path as a comment on the first line when the artifact represents a specific file. Avoid inventing APIs that weren't described in the task — if unsure, note the assumption instead of guessing silently.
